topic: Ransomware detection, prevention, and incident response - systematic literature review (PRISMA-style)
item: D. Explainability, reproducibility and benchmark validity - XAI (LIME/SHAP), replicability systematizations, dataset limitations

title.value: XRan: Explainable deep learning-based ransomware detection using dynamic analysis
Explainability in AI-based behavioral malware detection systems

authors.value: Gulmez, S.; Gorgulu Kakisim, A.; Sogukpinar, I.
Galli, A.; La Gatta, V.; Moscato, V.; Postiglione, M.; Sperli, G.

journal.value: Computers & Security, vol. 141, art. 103842 (Elsevier, open access)

quartile_sjr.value: Q1 (Scimago SJR 2024 = 1.445; Computer Science (miscellaneous) and Law; ISSN 0167-4048)
Q1 (Scimago SJR 2024 = 1.445; Computer Science (miscellaneous) and Law; ISSN 0167-4048)

study_type.value: Empirical experiment with XAI-enabled detection system design

methodology.value: Dynamic analysis in Cuckoo Sandbox extracting API-call sequences, DLL sequences, and mutex (mutual-exclusion) sequences combined into a multi-view feature space; two-layer CNN classifier; LIME (local) and SHAP (global) explanations of detection outcomes; five datasets: RD1 (VirusShare, 6,263 ransomware), RD2 (Sorel-20M, 7,703 ransomware), RD3 (ISOT, 668 ransomware), MD (VX Heaven, 6,263 malware), BD (Windows system files + Download.com, 14,797 benign)

XAI framework for API-call-sequence behavioral malware detection; evaluates four XAI methods (SHAP, LIME, LRP, and Attention mechanism) as explanatory layers for recurrent deep detectors (LSTM and GRU) across three API-call benchmark datasets differing in size, sequence length, and number of classes; compares effectiveness and efficiency of each XAI method per configuration

key_findings.value: XRan attains up to 99.4% True Positive Rate and outperforms baseline and state-of-the-art ransomware detectors; combining API/DLL/mutex sequence views preserves sequence relationships that frequency-domain-only features lose; LIME and SHAP consistently identify the dynamic features driving ransomware classification, giving analysts insight into the detection rationale

Each of SHAP, LIME, LRP, and Attention exhibits distinct effectiveness/efficiency trade-offs that vary with dataset size, sequence length, and class count; no single XAI method dominates across all behavioral malware detection formulations; embedding XAI makes AI-based behavioral detection more actionable for real-world SOC use, but black-box opacity remains an adoption barrier

limitations.value: Dynamic feature extraction incurs high runtime overhead; detection requires executing the binary in a Cuckoo sandbox, so fast or environment-sensitive ransomware activity may complete before capture; evaluation is Windows-centric; sandbox-based dynamic analysis is itself detectable and evadable by sophisticated families

Scope is generic malware rather than ransomware-specific; the datasets are proprietary and the authors state they do not have permission to share data, which blocks third-party replication and typifies the dataset-limitation problem this review item targets; explanation quality is sensitive to dataset characteristics

research_gaps.value: Addresses the explainability gap of black-box detectors for security analysts; notes that feature-extraction overhead and sandbox dependence remain unresolved for production deployment, and that XAI-guided insight into ransomware behavior (beyond accuracy) is an emerging requirement

Identifies the gap of choosing among XAI methods for security pipelines: no uniform guidance on which explanation method suits which data profile; future work on explanation faithfulness/fidelity validation and on larger, shareable datasets to support XAI evaluation at scale

inclusion_rationale.value: 2024 publication in Computers & Security (SJR 2024 = 1.445, Q1) indexed in ScienceDirect and Scopus; squarely in scope as an XAI (LIME/SHAP) ransomware detection study; no eligibility criterion failed.

Three API-call sequence datasets differing in size, sequence length, and number of classes; explicitly NOT shared (ScienceDirect data-availability statement: 'the authors do not have permission to share data')

Effectiveness and efficiency of four XAI methods (SHAP, LIME, LRP, Attention) per dataset/architecture; exact F1/accuracy values: [uncertain]

reproducibility.value: Benchmarked against multiple baseline and state-of-the-art detection methods; evaluation in a controlled Cuckoo sandbox rather than real infected-host environments; no external third-party evaluation; code and dataset publication: [uncertain]

Open-access (CC license) and methodologically detailed, but datasets are proprietary and not shared, so full third-party replication of the pipeline is not currently possible; compares model variants internally rather than against real-environment deployments
